item.title: Gold slides over 2.5% to yearly lows as risk-off mood offers little support
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) plunges more than 2.5% on Friday, hitting fresh year-to-date lows.

item.title: Euro retreats despite stronger GDP and hawkish ECB signals
item.description: EUR/USD turns lower on Friday, giving up earlier gains as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds amid heightened volatility across financial markets. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1140 after reaching an intraday high of 1.1214.

item.title: European Central Bank: December hike still base case – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Lee Sue Ann notes that the European Central Bank (ECB) kept key rates unchanged in October but delivered a hawkish message.

item.title: Norges Bank: Rate path seen steady – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Kjetil Olsen expects Norges Bank to keep its key policy rate at 4.5% next Thursday, in line with the September rate path. He notes mixed data: slightly higher core inflation and energy prices versus a stronger NOK and softer retail sales. Olsen argues communication will stay broadly unchanged and that rate cuts are unlikely before inflation clearly converges to the 2% target, which he does not foresee before 2028.

item.title: Bank of England: Gradual hiking path – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Stefan Koopman expects the Bank of England’s (BoE) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to raise Bank Rate to 4.00% in November 2026 in a 7-2 split, followed by another 25bp hike to 4.25% in February 2027. The report stresses that higher market rates have already tightened conditions, but argues policymakers must now validate pricing. Fiscal policy is seen as a minor offset to the energy-driven inflation shock.
